title: QUIC xquic Non-Handshake Residual Trace Verification
verification_method: Trace artifact review, requirement-home tests, preserved runner evidence review, captured packet replay, post-burst credit-burst replay, non-promoting runner diagnostic tests, and SpecTrace validation.
preconditions: The generated RFC 8999/9000/9001/9002 requirement coverage triage remains clean.
The generic ordered-read wake-up and delayed-ACK threshold issues remain closed by their focused proof.
The xquic residual evidence bundles remain preserved under `.artifacts/interop-runner`.
scope: Verify that the xquic client-role transfer/keyupdate/chacha20 residual has explicit trace ownership and a conservative proof boundary before runtime behavior changes are promoted.
procedure: Review `SPEC-QUIC-INT.json` and confirm `REQ-QUIC-INT-0029` links to this verification artifact.
Review `REQUIREMENT-GAPS.md` and `docs/current-status.md` to confirm the xquic residual points at the new trace set.
Run the focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-INT-0029`, including the captured xquic client packet replay that opens packet number 13 and verifies an ACK for xquic response packet 17.
Run the multi-packet captured xquic replay that opens client packet numbers 13 through 28 and verifies repeated MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAM_DATA credit publication after the response packet 17 ACK.

Run the interop runner helper failure-summary test that keeps the xquic timeout failed while adding the early-ACK-only post-burst diagnostic and the xquic short-header packet-processing ceiling through packets 0..3.
expected_result: The residual remains open but trace-owned, with current evidence paths, advisory boundaries, captured-packet ACK proof, repeated post-burst credit publication proof, and a non-promoting runner diagnostic recorded before any follow-up runtime fix is attempted.
status_summary: Passed for trace ownership, captured packet classification, repeated post-burst credit publication, and non-promoting runner diagnostics only. The current proof shows the managed client emitted a decryptable post-burst ACK for xquic response packet 17 and then emitted an alternating MAX_DATA/MAX_STREAM_DATA sequence through packet 28 with increasing limits. The helper preserves the xquic timeout as failed while preserving packet/key evidence that confirms valid post-burst ACK traffic, and the preserved May 19 all-upstream streamdata/keyupdate local run shows transfer, keyupdate, and chacha20 all timing out after 35,400 bytes at the response-stream FIN boundary. The fresh May 23 live rerun under `debug-client-transfer-xquic-live-refresh` again stopped after 15,355 bytes while the xquic server log reached `xqc_process_read_streams|stream_read_notify|flag:66` after the request stream was fully received and then stalled after the response burst at `xqc_send_packet_pacer_allows|pacing blocked` on `stream_offset:16536` before draining to FIN. The fresh May 23 keyupdate/chacha20 live rerun under `debug-client-keyupdate-chacha20-xquic-live-refresh` also stopped after 15,355 bytes, keeping the newer runtime evidence aligned across transfer, keyupdate, and chacha20. This does not close xquic liveness until a later runtime/test-backed slice supplies focused positive and negative proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This trace set does not claim xquic support, broad non-handshake all-upstream support, HTTP/3 coverage, or support readiness.

supplemental_sections.heading: May 23 packet classification
supplemental_sections.content: The embedded captured-packet proof uses CLIENT_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0 from the May 22 focused rerun and the xquic server short-header destination connection ID to open client packet number 13. The payload contains an ACK with largest acknowledged packet 17, an additional ACK range covering 0-11, and a MAX_DATA frame, which narrows the next investigation away from missing ACK emission.

supplemental_sections.heading: May 23 credit burst
supplemental_sections.content: The multi-packet replay opens client packet numbers 13 through 28 from the May 22 focused rerun and verifies strictly increasing MAX_DATA and MAX_STREAM_DATA values, alternating by packet, after the packet 17 ACK. That narrows the residual away from missing local credit publication while keeping xquic support unpromoted.

supplemental_sections.heading: Runner diagnostic
supplemental_sections.content: The local runner helper detects the preserved xquic early-ACK-only timeout shape from server logs plus managed client timeout output and appends a diagnostic to the failure reason without changing the non-zero exit result. When the server log exposes received short-header packet processing, the diagnostic also reports the processed client packet ceiling through packets 0..3 so future runs point at xquic event-loop packet consumption instead of local ACK, packet-protection, or credit-publication changes.

supplemental_sections.heading: May 19 shared ceiling
supplemental_sections.content: The preserved May 19 all-upstream streamdata/keyupdate local run shows the same 35,400-byte response-stream FIN ceiling across transfer, keyupdate, and chacha20. That keeps the residual shared across the non-handshake cells instead of isolating it to the later fresh transfer-only reruns.

supplemental_sections.heading: May 23 shared ceiling
supplemental_sections.content: The fresh May 23 keyupdate/chacha20 live rerun also stops after 15,355 bytes, matching the fresh transfer run's ceiling and keeping the newest runtime evidence aligned across the xquic non-handshake cells.

supplemental_sections.heading: May 23 server handoff
supplemental_sections.content: The fresh live rerun reached `xqc_process_read_streams|stream_read_notify|flag:66` after the request stream was fully received, and the preserved server log shows the response burst running through packet 22 before `xqc_send_packet_pacer_allows|pacing blocked` at `stream_offset:16536` prevented the transfer from draining to FIN. That narrows the current residual toward post-send drain, pacing wakeup, and stream-drain behavior rather than packet opening or local ACK emission.
